t: The Signature Vision: Asteroid Mining Robots
title: The Signature Vision: Asteroid Mining Robots
definition: The JAH-original Signature vision of Asteroid Mining Robots.
description:
The Signature vision of Asteroid Mining Robots does not ask what committees will fund — it asks what physics allows and what engineering can compound.

Signature robot hulls program, charter one: master miner bots at laboratory scale within the decade. Charter two: scale robot logistics manufacturing until cost collapses. Charter three: operate ore processing systems continuously, learning in public, improving every cycle.

This is a Signature concept — original JAH speculation, fully specified and honestly labeled. The public edition of this database carries the documented research record; this edition carries the bolder integrated vision: what Asteroid Mining Robots becomes when every piece is designed to work with every other piece from day one.

t: 2030 — First robot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
title: 2030 — First robot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses
definition: 2030 milestone on the Asteroid Mining Robots roadmap.
description:
First robot hulls fleets work unsupervised in warehouses, farms and low-g anchoring construction sites.

What must be true first: the miner bots results have to replicate outside the lab, robot logistics manufacturing must reach pilot scale, and ore processing operations need a year of continuous runtime. Miss any one and the date slips — that is the honest mechanics of forecasting. The Signature timeline pulls this earlier by integrating the pieces from day one.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed miner bots demonstrations, robot logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting ore processing uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: Readiness Estimator: Asteroid Mining Robots
definition: Estimates Asteroid Mining Robots readiness from component maturity.
description:
The estimator scores the six Asteroid Mining Robots components on the TRL 1–9 scale and averages them into a verdict: research phase, pilot phase, or deployment phase. Scores derive from the component records in this database — change a component's maturity and the verdict moves.

Honest scoring is the point: a robot hulls that averages TRL 3 is not failing, it is three phases from deployment, and the estimator tells you which component drags the average down. Fund that one first.

title: Asteroid Mining Robots Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates Asteroid Mining Robots operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a Asteroid Mining Robots installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 14781 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where miner bots monitoring, robot logistics redundancy, or ore processing maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: Asteroid Mining Robots Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for Asteroid Mining Robots: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for Asteroid Mining Robots — robots mining asteroids for materials.

Phase 1 — Prove (miner bots): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (robot logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (ore processing): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (low-g anchoring): robot hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and asteroids-scale deployment begins.

Signature edition: phases overlap aggressively — integration starts on day one. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.

Each phase has exit criteria.
Unites all 20 records.
